original.target_description: MIE recognition test 20–26 hours after scanning; 12 adults; overall recognition accuracy for high-reward versus low-reward scenes, paired one-tailed t test.

n.quote: Twenty to 26 hours after scanning, subjects (n = 12)
n.sample_role: Participants in the target within-subject recognition test.
n.exclusions: p. 515, Data Quality Assessment and Preprocessing: two scanned subjects excluded for behavioral noncompliance (eyes closed during low-value trials; misunderstood recognition rules); four excluded for motion (one) or sustained image artifacts (three). The target behavioral test explicitly reports n = 12.

es.quote: recognition accuracy was greater for high-reward than low-reward scenes [t(11) = 2.14, p = 0.03, one-tailed].

replication.target_description: Experiment 1; scene-recognition hit rates at 24-hour delay following high- versus low-reward encoding cues; mixed ANOVA main effect of reward across younger and older adults, F(1, 71). No scanning in this replication.

n.location: p. 732 (advance-access PDF p. 3), Table 1, Experiment 1, N row; p. 734 (PDF p. 5), Hit rates, F(1, 71)
n.sample_role: Participants: 36 younger adults and 37 older adults, respectively; both age groups included in target mixed ANOVA. Counts retained as printed by group.
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions stated in the paper. General Method describes health, vision/hearing and MMSE screening. p. 733 (PDF p. 4): first four encoding trials excluded as primacy buffers; first eight recognition trials excluded, leaving 240 recognition trials per participant (60 high-reward targets, 60 low-reward targets, 120 distractors).

es.location: p. 734 (advance-access PDF p. 5), Recognition performance, Hit rates

p.location: p. 734 (advance-access PDF p. 5), Recognition performance, Hit rates

reported_success.quote: This replicates Adcock and colleagues’ (2006) finding that intentional memory formation is boosted by the anticipation of uncertain remote rewards

notes: Both retrieved full-text titles and DOIs match the supplied references. Replication locator p. 734 identifies Experiment 1. With no subgroup specified, extracted its primary mixed-ANOVA reward effect across both age groups, rather than either follow-up age-specific t test. Replication effect size is the printed partial eta squared, with the corresponding F statistic retained; no metric conversion performed. Original extraction is the overall recognition-accuracy contrast, rather than the separate high-confidence-response contrast. Replication PDF is advance-access pagination (pages 1–11), mapped to journal pages 730–740. Quotes normalize PDF line breaks and the typesetting of partial eta squared.
